text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer reports lower test consumption (21.9 vs 26.8 kWh/100 km) and longer test range (367 vs 335 km) than the BMW i5 M60, though the article's own figures are partly inconsistent. Reviewer notes the lower maximum charging power of 180 kW against 205 kW for the BMW i5. Reviewer states the ET7 matches the i5 M60 to 100 km/h (3.8 s) but is slowest to 200 km/h (17.1 vs 12.9 s) and tops out at 200 vs 230 km/h. Reviewer states the ET7 is less dynamic than the German rivals including the BMW i5. Reviewer states the steering is too light in Comfort and too heavy in Sport+. Reviewer measured longer braking distances from 100 km/h than the BMW (35.7/35.1 m vs 33.4/32.2 m cold/warm). Reviewer states the air suspension delivers high comfort. Reviewer states rear legroom is larger than in the BMW, although the BMW offers the best rear headroom in the test. Reviewer notes a 363-litre boot against 490 litres for the BMW i5. Reviewer notes the rear seat does not fold. Reviewer praises the high-quality interior materials. Reviewer highlights rear-seat ventilation and generous equipment. Reviewer criticises that steering wheel and mirror adjustment are only possible via the touchscreen. Reviewer notes the absence of Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Reviewer states infotainment has improved since 2021 and NOMI voice control is more useful, but it is sometimes irritating. Reviewer notes the ET7 costs about PLN 409,900 against about PLN 500,000 for the BMW i5 M60.
